about.title: Chino Hills Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: A workplace injury in Chino Hills does not always happen inside a building. Plenty of people here earn a living behind the wheel, running deliveries along Chino Hills Parkway, hauling materials up Carbon Canyon Road, or commuting between job sites on SR-71. In 2025 the city recorded 96 injury collisions and 131 people hurt, with reports clustering on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., right when many shifts end. Some of those injured were on the clock. Others were hurt on construction sites, in warehouses, or at retail counters across town. Under California law, workers' compensation is usually your only claim against your employer, and fault does not matter. What many people miss is the second path: if a subcontractor, property owner, equipment manufacturer, or another driver contributed to what happened, a separate injury claim may be available. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Chino Hills workers with an independent attorney who can sort out which claims apply, at no cost unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Chino Hills Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We look past workers' comp
items.desc: Workers' compensation is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but it is not always the whole story. An attorney in our network can check whether a subcontractor, property owner, equipment maker, or another driver opens a separate claim.

items.title: Deadlines are tracked from day one
items.desc: California expects you to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days, and any third-party claim carries a 2-year deadline. Getting connected early keeps both clocks in view.

items.title: Retaliation is not something you have to absorb
items.desc: It is illegal for an employer to punish you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. If that is happening, the attorney you are matched with can address it alongside your injury case.

items.question: I was rear-ended on SR-71 while driving for my employer. Is that a workers' comp case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Because you were working, workers' compensation generally covers your medical care and part of your lost wages no matter who caused the crash. Separately, the other driver is a third party, so you may also have a personal injury claim against them with a 2-year filing deadline. An attorney can pursue the two together so nothing falls through the gap.

items.question: Does filing a workers' comp claim mean I cannot sue anyone?
items.answer: It means you usually cannot sue your employer, since workers' comp is the exclusive remedy against them regardless of fault. It does not shield outside parties. If a subcontractor, a property owner, or a defective piece of equipment played a role, a separate injury claim may still be open to you.

items.question: What if more than 30 days have passed since I got hurt at work in Chino Hills?
items.answer: Do not assume the door is closed. The 30-day window is for notifying your employer, and there are situations where a late report can still be accepted, especially if the employer already knew about the injury. Any third-party claim runs on its own 2-year deadline. The sooner you talk with an attorney, the more options remain.
